claim_verdicts.evidence: PG17 5.5.4: 'A primary key constraint indicates that a column, or group of columns, can be used as a unique identifier for rows in the table. This requires that the values be both unique and not null.' 'Primary keys can span more than one column'. CREATE TABLE: 'The PRIMARY KEY constraint specifies that a column or columns of a table can contain only unique (non-duplicate), nonnull values.'

Behaviour part: PG17 5.5.5 'NO ACTION means that if any referencing rows still exist when the constraint is checked, an error is raised; this is the default behavior if you do not specify anything.' 'Analogous to ON DELETE there is also ON UPDATE which is invoked when a referenced column is changed (updated).' Schema line 20 has no ON UPDATE. Rule part: 5.5 has no statement that key values must not change; the rule is outline item 1's, given with its reason.
claim_verdicts.source: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/ddl-constraints.html (5.5.5); examples/don-hang@stage-0 db/schema.sql line 20; track.yaml outline item 1

claim_verdicts.evidence: PG17 5.5.5: 'A foreign key constraint specifies that the values in a column (or a group of columns) must match the values appearing in some row of another table.' 'A foreign key must reference columns that either are a primary key or form a unique constraint, or are columns from a non-partial unique index.' 'Normally, a referencing row need not satisfy the foreign key constraint if any of its referencing columns are null.' All five REFERENCES (schema lines 20, 27, 28, 36, 44) name (id), the PRIMARY KEY.

schema line 20 'customer_id integer NOT NULL REFERENCES customers (id)': one column, NOT NULL, no UNIQUE. seed lines 24, 25, 33: orders 1, 2 and 10 all have customer_id 1. FK rule as in claim 4 (PG17 5.5.5).

PG17 5.5.5: 'A table can have more than one foreign key constraint. This is used to implement many-to-many relationships between tables. Say you have tables about products and orders, but now you want to allow one order to contain possibly many products'; its order_items example has 'product_no integer REFERENCES products' and 'order_id integer REFERENCES orders'. Schema lines 27-28: order_items.order_id REFERENCES orders (id), product_id REFERENCES products (id).

schema line 13 customers 'full_name text NOT NULL'; orders (lines 18-24) holds only id, customer_id, placed_at, status; no other table has a customer-name column. PG17 docs give no definition of normalisation; the one-line definition restates outline item 4, and depth_notes exclude formal normal forms.

Verified part: schema.sql has six CREATE TABLE (lines 4, 11, 18, 26, 34, 42); the diagram draws customers, orders, order_items, products with a subset of columns whose types match the schema. Unverified part: that '||' means exactly one and 'o{' zero or more, restating the labels, is Mermaid notation; Mermaid has no key or docs root in versions.yaml and no mirror in refs/, so no allowed source settles it. Kind fact: not blocking.
claim_verdicts.source: examples/don-hang@stage-0 db/schema.sql; content/versions.yaml (no mermaid key); refs/ (no Mermaid mirror)

claim_verdicts.evidence: PG17 CREATE TABLE synopsis: 'column_name data_type [ ... ] [ column_constraint [ ... ] ]'; column_constraint lists NOT NULL, CHECK ( expression ), GENERATED { ALWAYS | BY DEFAULT } AS IDENTITY, UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY, REFERENCES reftable [ ( refcolumn ) ]. PG17 4.1: 'Tokens are normally separated by whitespace (space, tab, newline)'; 'commands can usefully be split across lines' (schema lines 22-23).

PG17 5.3: 'An identity column is a special column that is generated automatically from an implicit sequence.' 'If an INSERT command is executed on the table with the identity column and no value is explicitly specified for the identity column, then a value generated by the implicit sequence is inserted.' 'If BY DEFAULT is selected, then the user-specified value takes precedence.' seed.sql inserts explicit ids, then calls setval on each sequence.

PG17 5.5.3: 'Unique constraints ensure that the data contained in a column, or a group of columns, is unique among all the rows in the table.' The null exemption ('two null values are not considered equal') cannot apply: schema line 14 'email text NOT NULL UNIQUE'. 5.5.4: 'A table can have at most one primary key.'; it is on id (line 12).

CREATE TABLE column_constraint 'REFERENCES reftable [ ( refcolumn ) ]'. PG17 5.5.5: 'a referencing row need not satisfy the foreign key constraint if any of its referencing columns are null'; NOT NULL on customer_id (schema line 20) removes that exemption, so every orders row must match a customer.

CREATE TABLE table_constraint: 'PRIMARY KEY ( column_name [, ... ] )'; 'only unique (non-duplicate), nonnull values'. PG17 5.5.4: 'Primary keys can span more than one column'. Schema line 31 'PRIMARY KEY (order_id, product_id)' is a table-constraint entry, not a column. Seed line 38 stores two units as one row '( 1, 2, 2,  450000)'.

seed line 37 'INSERT INTO order_items (order_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price_vnd) VALUES', line 38 '( 1, 1, 1, 1250000), ( 1, 2, 2,  450000),'. schema line 1: 'Money is stored in whole đồng, so every amount is an integer.' Product 2's price_vnd is 450000 (seed line 7).

Facts hold: schema line 7 products.price_vnd and line 30 order_items.unit_price_vnd are separate columns with no REFERENCES between them; payment 1 (seed line 52) 2150000 = 1250000 + 2 x 450000. But 'its name gives it a different job' is not supportable: a column name assigns nothing, and the repo states no purpose (git grep 'unit_price' at stage-0 hits only schema.sql, seed.sql, db/queries/transaction-place-order.sql, none with a comment on it).
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: `unit_price_vnd` looks like a copy of `products.price_vnd`, but it is a separate column on each order item, so every item keeps its own price per unit: what this order was charged. When a product's price can change later, old orders must keep what they cost, so that fact belongs to the order item.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Design recommendation carrying its condition ('When a product's price can change later'), so not opinion-as-fact. PG17 5.5 (fetched) says nothing about price history; the repo gives no rationale for unit_price_vnd (see claim 15). Kind opinion: does not block.

Hedged in section 6 ('usually kept for a slowdown you have measured, and you then own keeping every copy in step'); quiz q4 c and q6 d explanations match it. No allowed source (PG17 docs root) addresses copying facts for speed. Kind opinion: does not block.
claim_verdicts.source: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/ddl-constraints.html (no statement on copying facts for speed)

claim_verdicts.evidence: PG17 5.5.5: 'NO ACTION means that if any referencing rows still exist when the constraint is checked, an error is raised; this is the default behavior if you do not specify anything.' CREATE TABLE: 'NO ACTION: Produce an error indicating that the deletion or update would create a foreign key constraint violation. ... This is the default action.' No REFERENCES in schema has ON DELETE/ON UPDATE. Not executed: Docker engine not running, no local psql.

Premises documented: PG17 5.5.4 'This requires that the values be both unique and not null' (a shared phone number cannot be a key); NO ACTION default refuses changing a referenced key while referencing rows exist (claim 18). Repo: customers 'id integer GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY', 'email text NOT NULL UNIQUE' (lines 12, 14). The recommendation carries its condition; the lesson's wording 'a key must do neither' is flagged as a separate issue.

schema lines 34-48: payments and notifications each have 'id integer GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY' and 'order_id integer NOT NULL REFERENCES orders (id)', one REFERENCES each, no UNIQUE on order_id. seed lines 62-63: notifications 1 and 2 both have order_id 1.

PG17 4.1.5: 'A comment is a sequence of characters beginning with double dashes and extending to the end of the line' and 'A comment is removed from the input stream before further syntax analysis and is effectively replaced by whitespace.' schema line 10 '-- lesson: foundation.l1.tables-keys-relations' is such a line.

PG17 Table 8.1: 'integer | int, int4 | signed four-byte integer'; 'text | | variable-length character string'; 'timestamp [ (p) ] with time zone | timestamptz | date and time, including time zone'. 8.1.1: 'The types smallint, integer, and bigint store whole numbers'. 8.5: 'timestamptz is accepted as an abbreviation for timestamp with time zone'; 'the value is stored internally as UTC, and the originally stated or assumed time zone is not retained.'

refs/docker-docs guides/postgresql.md line 414: 'If the directory is empty, the container runs initdb to create a new database cluster, then executes all scripts in /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/ in alphabetical order before starting PostgreSQL.' docker-compose.yml@stage-0 lines 67-68 mount schema.sql as 10-schema.sql and seed.sql as 20-seed.sql, so the schema runs first.

issues.quote: PostgreSQL rejects a row whose `id` has no value (`NULL`)
issues.text: orders.id is an identity column: an INSERT that gives no id is not rejected, PostgreSQL fills it (PG17 5.3: 'no value is explicitly specified ... a value generated by the implicit sequence is inserted'), which section 5 itself says ('fill it with the next number when a new row arrives without one'). Only an explicit NULL is refused. Read in order, sections 4 and 5 contradict each other.
issues.fix: Section 4: replace 'PostgreSQL rejects a row whose `id` has no value (`NULL`) or repeats' with 'PostgreSQL never stores a row whose `id` is empty (`NULL`) or repeats'. Keep the rest of the sentence.

issues.quote: but its name gives it a different job: the price per unit this order was charged
issues.text: Claim 15 rephrased. A column name assigns no job, and the repo states no purpose for unit_price_vnd (no comment in schema.sql, seed.sql or transaction-place-order.sql). What is supportable is that it is a separate column on each order item.
issues.fix: Replace the sentence with claim 15's suggested_text: '`unit_price_vnd` looks like a copy of `products.price_vnd`, but it is a separate column on each order item, so every item keeps its own price per unit: what this order was charged.' Mirror in quiz q4 explanation 'correct' (en and vi), which repeats 'The name of `unit_price_vnd` gives it a different job'.

issues.quote: a meaningful value can change or be shared, and a key must do neither
issues.text: Only 'not shared' is enforced (PG17 5.5.4: values 'both unique and not null'). Nothing in PG17 forbids changing a key value; 5.5.5 provides ON UPDATE CASCADE, where 'the updated values of the referenced column(s) should be copied into the referencing row(s)'. 'Must not change' is outline item 1's design rule, stated here as if it were a database rule.
issues.fix: Section 6: 'a meaningful value can change or be shared; a key can never be shared, and should not change, because other tables store it'. Apply the same split in quiz q2 explanation d ('a key must do neither') and q5 explanation d ('a key must neither change nor be shared'), en and vi.

issues.quote: when a customer changes number and the update fails
issues.text: With NO ACTION the update fails only 'if any referencing rows still exist' (PG17 5.5.5). A customer with no orders (seed: customer 5) can have the key changed without error. The preceding sentence carries the condition ('while their orders still hold the old one'); this one drops it.
issues.fix: Replace with 'when a customer who has orders changes number and the update fails.'

issues.quote: each line's label, repeated in symbols at its ends, says how many rows sit on each side
issues.text: Claim 8 unverified: what '||' and 'o{' mean, and that they restate the labels, is Mermaid notation; Mermaid has no key in content/versions.yaml and no mirror in refs/, so no allowed source settles it. Kind fact, not blocking.
issues.fix: Cut 'repeated in symbols at its ends,' so the clause reads 'each line's label says how many rows sit on each side', and drop the end-mark part from claim 8; or have the owner add a Mermaid key with a docs root to content/versions.yaml.

issues.quote: a column whose value must equal the key of a row in the table it points at, unless the row leaves it with no value; in Đơn Hàng that key is always the primary key
issues.text: Had to re-read this twice. 'the row' could mean the row holding the foreign key or the row pointed at, and 'the key of a row' suggests keys other than the primary key exist, which the lesson never shows (later `email` is UNIQUE 'yet it is not the key', so I wonder whether it is some other kind of key).
issues.fix: Replace 'unless the row leaves it with no value' with 'unless this column is left with no value', and 'the key of a row' with 'a value that identifies one row'.

issues.quote: so the first `1` in the seed line names exactly one order
issues.text: The lesson never says that the values in a seed line follow the order of the table's columns. The diagram shows three columns of `orders` while the seed line has four values, so I only confirmed that the first value is `id` and the second is `customer_id` after seeing the CREATE TABLE block in section 5.
issues.fix: Add one sentence before 'In the situation above, the primary key of `orders` is `id`.' saying that each value in the seed line fills one column of `orders`, in order: `id`, `customer_id`, the time, the status.

issues.quote: With foreign keys written like Đơn Hàng's, it also refuses to change a customer's `id` while an order holds it
issues.text: 'written like Đơn Hàng's' implies foreign keys can be written another way that behaves differently, but the lesson never says what that way is. I stopped to wonder whether the refusal is a rule of all foreign keys or a choice made in Đơn Hàng. It does not block the main idea, and q5 removes the doubt by saying 'exactly as db/schema.sql writes it'.
issues.fix: Replace 'With foreign keys written like Đơn Hàng's, it also refuses' with 'The foreign key as `db/schema.sql` writes it also makes PostgreSQL refuse', so the sentence points at code the reader will see in section 5.

issues.quote: then rules every row must pass; the rule on `status` continues on the next line
issues.text: `CHECK (...)` appears four times across the two blocks but is never named. From 'rules every row must pass' I can guess that `CHECK (price_vnd > 0)` is such a rule and that `status IN (...)` means 'one of these values', but I am guessing. Quiz q4 option d's explanation then relies on 'only its own `CHECK`'.
issues.fix: Extend the sentence to: 'then rules every row must pass, such as `NOT NULL` (the column must have a value) or `CHECK (price_vnd > 0)` (the value must make the condition true)'.

issues.quote: `unit_price_vnd` looks like a copy of `products.price_vnd`, but its name gives it a different job
issues.text: A name cannot give a column a job; what makes it a different fact is that it holds the price charged when the order was placed. Read literally, I could conclude that renaming a copied column stops it being a copy, which clashes with the first 'Beginners often think' item. Quiz q4's correct explanation repeats 'The name of `unit_price_vnd` gives it a different job'.
issues.fix: Replace 'but its name gives it a different job:' with 'but it records a different fact:' in the lesson, and make the same change to the opening of q4's correct explanation (en and vi).
